[Figure B-1] SIGNAL: EXTEND or LOWER STRUT(S) | FROM: Director | TO: Pilot | Day: Extend arms to one side, palms together and horizontal. Then, open arms. | Night: Same except hold wands horizontally. | Note: For lowering strut, reverse the procedure for extending strut.

[Figure B-1] SIGNAL: LOWER LAUNCH BAR/TOW LINK | FROM: Director | TO: Deck Crew, Pilot | Day: Rest right elbow in left palm at waist level. Bring right hand down to horizontal position. | Night: Same except with wands.

[Figure B-1] SIGNAL: RAISE LAUNCH BAR/TOW LINK | FROM: Director | TO: Deck Crew, Pilot | Day: Rest right elbow in left palm at waist level. With right forearm horizontal, bring right hand up to shoulder level. | Night: Same as day except rest right elbow on wand.

[Figure B-1] SIGNAL: TENSION AIRCRAFT ON CATAPULT (drawings: Day, Night) | FROM: Director | TO: Catapult Crew, Pilot | Day: Extend arms overhead. Open clenched fists, palms forward to indicate pilot release brakes. Then sweep one hand across chest and point in direction of launch. Pilot will release brakes and apply appropriate power in accordance with aircraft NATOPS Manual. | Night: Same using wands except indicate pilot release brakes by opening crossed wands above head.

[Figure B-2] SIGNAL: UNTENSION AIRCRAFT ON CATAPULT (drawings: Day, Night) | FROM: Launching Officer | TO: Catapult Crew, Pilot | Day: Extend arms overhead, fists clenched to indicate pilot hold brakes. Then sweep one fist across chest and point in opposite direction of launch. Pilot will hold brakes. | Night: Hold wands crossed overhead to indicate pilot hold brakes. Then sweep one wand across chest and point in opposite direction of launch. Pilot will hold brakes.

[Figure B-2] SIGNAL: FIRST TURNUP (drawings: Day, Night) | FROM: Launching Officer | TO: Pilot | Day: Extend arm overhead, forefinger pointing up. Hesitate, then rotate hand rapidly in a horizontal circle. | Night: Hold RED and GREEN wands at chest level, rotating the green wand in a horizontal circle. | Remarks: Signal is optional, given at request of pilot. Also can be used for deck launch.

[Figure B-3] SIGNAL: AFTERBURNER (drawings: Day, Night) | FROM: Launching Officer | TO: Pilot | Day: Give "final turnup" signal (no. 9). Wait 2 or 3 seconds while pilot turns up to military rated thrust and checks instruments. Then, hold open hand toward pilot, fingers extended vertically. | Night: Same except hold GREEN wand vertically and move up and down. | Remarks: Pilot select afterburner, check instruments, and: 1. Day — Salute when ready to launch. 2. Night — turn on only his running lights (STEADY), and keep them on until clear of the ship.

[Figure B-3] SIGNAL: FIRE/LAUNCH (drawings: Day, Night) | FROM: Launching Officer | TO: Catapult Crew, Pilot | Day: Extend arm overhead. Ensure that pilot's head is against headrest and deck is clear forward. Sweep up-raised hand downward in the direction of launch, touching the deck and returning hand to the horizontal in the direction of launch | Night: Raise GREEN wand vertically overhead. Wait 2 or 3 seconds for pilot to position head against headrest. Ensure that deck is clear forward. Sweep wand in a wide arc, ending by pointing in the direction of launch, touching the deck and returning wand to the horizontal in the direction of launch. | WARNING: The launching officer shall remain in the crouched position with his hand/wand held horizontally in the direction of launch until the aircraft has passed his position or a suspend/hangfire situation is indicated. | Note: Also used for free deck launches.

[Figure B-4] SIGNAL: SUSPEND (drawings: Day, Night) | FROM: Launching Officer | TO: Catapult Crew, Pilot | Day: Cross arms overhead indicating the launch is off. | Night: Hold RED wand high overhead indicating the launch is off. GREEN wand is turned off. | Remarks: After this signal, pilot must remain ready for launch and not throttle back until after the "untension" and "throttle back" signals are given by the launching officer/catapult safety observer (ICCS). | Note: Any flight deck or catapult personnel may signal a SUSPEND to the launching officers. The DAY signal is the same as the launching officer's. The NIGHT signal is a horizontal movement of a wand or light.

[Figure B-4] SIGNAL: HANGFIRE (drawings: Day, Night) | FROM: Launching Officer/Catapult Safety Observer (ICCS) | TO: Catapult Crew, Pilot | Day: Give "suspend" signal (no. 12). Then point index finger of one hand at palm of other hand. | Night: Give "suspend" signal (no. 12). Then hold RED wand overhead in a horizontal position. GREEN wand remains off.

[Figure B-5] SIGNAL: UNTENSION AIRCRAFT ON CATAPULT (Following suspend or hangfire) (drawings: Day, Night) | FROM: Launching Officer; Catapult Safety Observer (ICCS) | TO: Catapult Crew; Launching Officer (ICCS) (printed as two lines side by side: Launching Officer - Catapult Crew, Catapult Safety Observer (ICCS) - Launching Officer (ICCS)) | Day: With arms in "suspend" or "hangfire" position, sweep one hand from above head across chest and point in opposite direction to launch. | Night: With RED wand in "suspend" or "hangfire" position, sweep it across chest and point in opposite direction of launch.

[Figure B-5] SIGNAL: THROTTLE BACK (drawings: Day, Night) | FROM: Launching Officer/Catapult Safety Observer (ICCS) | TO: Pilot | Day: Hold one fist at waist level, thumb extended up. Grasp thumb with other hand and rock as if adjusting throttle. | Night: Hold RED wand horizontally across chest. Raise and lower horizontal wand. GREEN wand is off.
[Figure B-5] SIGNAL: PUSH/PULL BACK | FROM: Director | TO: Deck Crew | Day: Make for-to-aft sweeping motion with arms extended downward, palms forward. | Night: Same except with wands.

[Figure B-6] SIGNAL: ACCEPT CONTROL (drawings: Day, Night) | FROM: Catapult Officer | TO: Director | Day: Hold both hands with fists clenched in front at waist height. | Night: Hold wands vertically in front of body. Turn wands on.

[Figure B-6] SIGNAL: PASS CONTROL (drawings: Day, Night) | FROM: Director | TO: Catapult Officer | Day: With both arms at shoulder height, point in direction of person receiving control. | Night: Same as day signal except point wands.

[Figure B-6] SIGNAL: RETRACT SHUTTLE | FROM: Catapult Officer | TO: Deckedge Operator | Day: Finger pointing towards the bow at waist level. Sweep arm in a complete large circular motion. Stopping the sweeping motion with the finger pointed aft at waist level. | Night: Same except use RED wand. | Remarks: Deckedge Operator retract shuttle.

[Figure B-6] SIGNAL: ADVANCE SHUTTLE | FROM: Catapult Officer | TO: Deckedge Operator | Day: Finger pointing aft at waist level. Sweep arm in a complete large circular motion. Stopping the sweeping motion with the finger pointed towards the bow at waist level. | Night: Same except use RED wand. | Remarks: Deckedge Operator retract shuttle.

[Figure B-7] SIGNAL: CLEAR DECK | FROM: Flight Deck Officer/Director | TO: Arresting Gear Officer | Day: Sweep arm from overhead position to side position and return. | Night: Same as day except with AMBER wand.
[Figure B-7] SIGNAL: FOUL DECK | FROM: Flight Deck Officer/Director | TO: Arresting Gear Officer | Day: Cross arms overhead, fists clenched. | Night: Crossed AMBER wands held overhead

[Figure B-7] SIGNAL: PULL BACK | FROM: Hook Runner | TO: Director | Day: Make fore-to-aft sweeping motion with arms extended downward, palms aft. | Night: Same motion except with RED stubby wand. || FROM: Director | TO: Pilot, Deckedge Operator | Day: Make fore-to-aft sweeping motion with arms extended, palms forward. | Night: Same motion except with two AMBER wands.
[Figure B-8] SIGNAL: CEASE PULL BACK | FROM: Director | TO: Deckedge Operator || FROM: Hook Runner | TO: Director | Day: Cross arms below waist | Night: Horizontal movements of wand below waist.

[Figure B-8] SIGNAL: RAISE HOOK | FROM: Director | TO: Pilot | Day: Position left hand horizontally in front of body, palm down. Move right hand upward, bringing extended thumb into left palm. | Night: Position left wand horizontally in front of body. Position right wand vertically to form a “T”.

[Figure B-9] SIGNAL: LOWER HOOK | FROM: Director | TO: Pilot | Day: Position left hand horizontally in front of body, palm up. Move right hand downward, bringing extended thumb into left palm. | Night: Position left wand horizontally in front of body. Position right wand vertically to form an inverted “T”.
[Figure B-9] SIGNAL: WIRE CLEAR | FROM: Hook Runner | TO: Director | Day: Make a vertical motion with arm pointed at the taxi director. | Night: Same, holding RED stubby wand.
[Figure B-9] SIGNAL: WIRE RETRACT | FROM: Hook Runner | TO: Deckedge Operator | Day: Make large circular motion with arm extended to one side. | Night: Same, holding RED stubby wand.

[Figure B-10] SIGNAL: TILLER BAR IN PLACE OR ENGAGE NOSEWHEEL STEERING | FROM: Director | TO: Pilot | Day: Touch end of nose with forefinger. Then, give thumbs up signal with same hand. | Night: Touch end of nose with wand. Then, give “up” signal with same wand.

[Figure B-10] SIGNAL: TILLER BAR REMOVED OR DISENGAGE NOSE WHEEL STEERING | FROM: Director | TO: Pilot | Day: Touch end of nose with forefinger. Then, sweep arm downward in direction of aircraft movement. | Night: Touch end of nose with wand. Then, sweep wand downward in direction of aircraft movement.
[Figure B-10] SIGNAL: INSTALL TIEDOWNS | FROM: Director | TO: Pilot, Brake Rider | Day: Rotate hands in a vertical circle in front of body. | Night: Same as day except with AMBER wands.
[Figure B-10] SIGNAL: TIEDOWNS IN PLACE | FROM: Director | TO: Pilot, Brake Rider | EXECUTION: Same as “Install Tiedowns” adding a thumbs up signal.

[Figure B-10] SIGNAL: REVERSE THRUST TAXI | FROM: Director | TO: Pilot | Day: Palms facing aircraft at eye level with a pushback motion. For turns, the director points in direction tail is to move. | Night: Same, holding wands.
[Figure B-11] REFUELING SIGNALS — TOP OFF (item number not printed legibly; only a faint mark precedes it, the other items are numbered 2.–7.): Pat top of head.
[Figure B-11] REFUELING SIGNALS — 2. FUEL STATUS: Movement of thumb to mouth for requesting fuel on board.
[Figure B-11] REFUELING SIGNALS — 3. PROBE OUT: Arm across chest, then extend out horizontally.
[Figure B-11] REFUELING SIGNALS — 4. PROBE IN: Arm extended out horizontally, then brought in to cross chest.
[Figure B-11] REFUELING SIGNALS — 5. CLOSE DUMP VALVE: Point finger at elbow.
[Figure B-11] REFUELING SIGNALS — 6. CUT FUEL: Fingers point at throat, moving hand sideways.
[Figure B-11] REFUELING SIGNALS — 7. FUEL WEIGHT STATUS: Movement of arms up and down, palms up for requesting fuel weights.

[Figure B-11] FUEL QUANTITY SIGNALS* — FOR HUNDREDS OF POUNDS: Clenched fist followed by 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 (drawings: 100–500 = one to five fingers raised vertically; 600–900 = hand held horizontally with one to four fingers extended).

[Figure B-11] FUEL QUANTITY SIGNALS* — FOR EVEN THOUSANDS OF POUNDS: 1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000, 5,000, 6,000, 7,000, 8,000, 9,000 (drawings: 1,000–5,000 = one to five fingers raised vertically; 6,000–9,000 = hand held horizontally with one to four fingers extended).

[Figure B-11] FUEL QUANTITY SIGNALS* — FOR LOADS THAT DO NOT FALL ON EVEN THOUSANDS OF POUNDS: Example: 1,500 lbs = 1,000 lbs followed by 500 lbs. Example: 7,400 lbs = 7,000 lbs followed by 400 lbs. Double finger (a vertical signal followed by a horizontal one) (drawings: 1,000 lbs = one finger vertical, 500 lbs = five fingers vertical; 7,000 lbs = two fingers horizontal, 400 lbs = four fingers vertical).

[Figure B-11] FUEL QUANTITY SIGNALS* — FOR LOADS OF TEN THOUSANDS OF POUNDS AND OVER: Example: 12,000 lbs = 10,000 lbs followed by 2,000 lbs followed by clenched fist. Example: 12,500 lbs = 10,000 lbs followed by 2,000 lbs followed by 500 lbs. Double finger (a vertical signal followed by a horizontal one) followed by a clenched fist for exact thousands, or a third finger signal for hundreds. (drawings: 10,000 lbs = one finger vertical; 2,000 lbs = two fingers vertical; 500 lbs = five fingers vertical).
[Figure B-11] Footnote: *NATO fuel signals can be found in Figure 1-1 (9 of 9) p. 1-11
